belief: Everyone from that group is the same.
origins: Stereotypes are learned early: from family jokes, news coverage, a bad experience, or a neighborhood’s attitudes. Our minds sort people into categories to save effort, and fear or hurt can harden those categories. The result is judging individuals by a label.
teaches: God told Samuel, “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart,” and Peter learned that God shows no favoritism. James writes, “do not show favoritism.” Genesis teaches, “God created man in His own image… male and female He created them.” Jesus welcomed a Samaritan woman and held up a Samaritan as the hero of a story; the Samaritan “had compassion.” Scripture insists that every person is an individual made in God’s image. Labels flatten what God made unique.
self_statements: You can’t trust any of them.
I know what those people are like.
One bad experience tells me everything.
I do not need to know them.
errors: Treating one person or experience as representing a group.
Noticing only what fits the stereotype.
Assuming I know what an individual thinks.
questions: Where did I first learn this idea about this group?
Do I know anyone from this group personally? What are they like?
Would I want someone to judge me by a label?
What exceptions have I noticed, and what does that suggest?
What does it mean that every person is made in God’s image?
How could I get to know one person as an individual?
truth: Every person is made in God’s image and is an individual. Labels hide the person God sees. I can examine my assumptions, listen, and treat people one by one.
hw_truths: Every person is made in God’s image.
Exceptions are not rare, they are the rule.
log: Each week, note one assumption you questioned and what you learned.
actions: Write what you think of the group and where it came from.
Look for counterexamples in your own experience.
Ask someone from the group about their life.
Pray by name for people you know.
prayer: Lord, forgive me for the ways I have lumped people together. Help me see each person as You see them, made in Your image, and let me love my neighbor with open eyes. Amen.
hw_questions: Whom do I know from this group?
What does image of God mean?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Every person is made in God’s image, so I will not judge by a label.”
